extracted.intended_audience: public relations practitioners, corporate communicators, PR students and advisers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for the professional public relations counsel on the scope, methods, audience-targeting, and ethical obligations of shaping public opinion and managing relations between organizations and their publics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of public relations
rubrics_metrics.description: The counsel on public relations "interprets the client to the public and the public to the client" and seeks "adjustment and understanding between enterprises and the people on whom they are dependent."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PR is a management function concerned with relations between an entity and its publics; it involves advising on formulation of attitudes and actions that will win public favor and procedures to bring them to public attention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Action plus education principle
rubrics_metrics.description: Good public relations depend not alone on words, but on action deserving public support, and education of the public to acquaint it with such action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PR work should combine substantive, socially defensible actions by the client with communication/education efforts; don't rely solely on publicity to cover for poor practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish PR from other practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Public relations differs widely from publicity, advertising, propaganda, promotion, exploitation and similar activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid conflating PR with mere advertising or propaganda; PR emphasizes mutual understanding and often includes advising on policy and behavior, not just message distribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand what constitutes public opinion
rubrics_metrics.description: Public opinion is a social product of interacting forces, groups and 'herd' mechanisms rather than purely individual reasoned judgment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study group psychology and the interacting forces that form opinion; accept that opinions are often compromises and operate at the level of the group's average intelligence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publics are groups — segment and target
rubrics_metrics.description: Classification of the public into groups (geographical divisions, professional divisions, business divisions, divisions of religion, economic position, preferences, etc.) is essential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify and classify target audiences precisely; tailor appeals to the right group segments rather than using one-size-fits-all messaging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use established mediums to reach the public
rubrics_metrics.description: "The Public Can Be Reached Only through Established Mediums of Communication."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose appropriate channels (press, radio, film, direct mail, newsreel, word of mouth, etc.); evaluate each medium's reach and suitability for the intended group.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leverage interlapping, shifting group formations
rubrics_metrics.description: The interlapping group formations of society, the continuous shifting of groups, and the flexibility of human nature are aids to the counsel on public relations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exploit overlaps and shifting affiliations to spread ideas across networks; recognize mobility in group boundaries when planning campaigns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use opinion leaders and word-of-mouth
rubrics_metrics.description: Word of mouth is an important medium; group leaders are strong factors in giving currency to ideas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify and enlist influential individuals and leaders in target groups to amplify messages and seed acceptance organically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classify publics for direct-by-mail and lists
rubrics_metrics.description: Direct-by-mail and printed word afford channels of approach; companies have lists classed by innumerable criteria for targeted appeals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain and use segmented mailing lists (geography, profession, economic status, religion, preferences) to deliver tailored materials. Include telegraphic/wireless where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose appropriate film/media formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Different film types exist: feature films (indirect), educational films (direct to arranged groups), and newsreels (controlled events).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select film/media format according to objective: use educational films for organized audiences, newsreels for event/value-driven exposure, features only indirectly as cultural inputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and publicity of facts
rubrics_metrics.description: Publicity defined as 'the making public, both to government authorities and to the public at large, the essential facts in which the public is concerned.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When appropriate, put essential facts into the public domain; the 'light of day' deters wrongdoing and builds credibility—use openness rather than secrecy when it serves the public interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid deception, appeals to falsehoods and prejudices
rubrics_metrics.description: Influencing opinion is legitimate provided efforts avoid 'the employment of falsehood,' appeals to 'prejudices' or 'passions,' and 'the proscription of those who will not fall in with particular opinions and practices.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use fabricated facts, manipulative appeals, or suppression of dissent; adhere to truthful communication and avoid stoking prejudices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical duty to society over client partisanship
rubrics_metrics.description: The public relations counsel must not accept a retainer or assume a position which puts his duty to the client above his duty to larger society and his own standards of integrity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refuse clients or assignments that would propagate unsocial, harmful or unethical movements even if legally defensible; evaluate social consequences before accepting work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judge results from an ethical point of view
rubrics_metrics.description: While not called upon to judge the merits like a court, the counsel must judge the results his work would accomplish from an ethical point of view.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anticipate downstream social effects of campaigns; do not undertake advocacy likely to cause public harm or to mislead in ways that damage public welfare.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid 'whitewash' and insincere defense
rubrics_metrics.description: Early publicity advisers often 'whitewashed' clients — merely obtaining newspaper space to defend business without recommending policy changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not simply spin or whitewash; where clients have unsocial practices, advise corrective action rather than merely defensive publicity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role as educator vs propagandist
rubrics_metrics.description: The difference between 'propaganda' and 'education' is largely point of view; advocacy of what we believe in is 'education' while what we don't believe in is 'propaganda.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strive for educational, fact-based advocacy that informs and elevates public debate rather than manipulative propaganda; be mindful of how labeling affects perception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand limits of public reasoning and crowd psychology
rubrics_metrics.description: Public opinion is often the product of crowd psychology and herd reaction; society cannot wait for absolute truth and adopts compromise 'truths.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design communications that work at the group's level of understanding; use simplified, repeatable messages that can compete in the 'marketplace of ideas.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Use history and precedent to inform tactics
rubrics_metrics.description: Historical examples (pamphlets, newspapers, theatre, ceremonies) show how leaders used media of their time to shape opinion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Learn from historical precedents in selecting tactics appropriate to current media ecosystems; adapt timeless persuasion techniques to contemporary channels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain professional standards and self-regulation
rubrics_metrics.description: The profession lacks formal legal gatekeepers; acceptance depends on professional conduct and the counsel's own standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt and uphold high standards of practice, participate in professional associations, and develop internal codes to legitimize the profession and protect public trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan for shifting media economics and press independence
rubrics_metrics.description: Newspapers and media shift economically (e.g., advertising influence); press independence affects the PR-press relationship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of media incentives, revenue models, and independence; cultivate credible relationships with press while avoiding undue influence or 'buying' coverage.
